Package dev.shvquu.betternpcs.api.event

Klasse NpcInteractEvent

java.lang.Object
org.bukkit.event.Event
dev.shvquu.betternpcs.api.event.NpcEvent
dev.shvquu.betternpcs.api.event.NpcInteractEvent
Alle implementierten Schnittstellen:
org.bukkit.event.Cancellable
public class NpcInteractEvent extends NpcEvent implements org.bukkit.event.Cancellable
Fired when a player clicks an NPC, before the NPC's configured actions run.

This one event covers every interaction — left click, right click and their sneaking variants — with getInteraction() saying which. Attacks arrive here as InteractionType.LEFT_CLICK; a separate NpcDamageEvent follows for NPCs that are not invulnerable, for listeners that care about damage specifically rather than about clicks.

Cancelling stops the configured actions from running. It does not stop other listeners, which should check isCancelled() themselves if they want to respect an earlier veto.

Clients send an interaction packet per click, so a player holding down a mouse button produces a stream of these. The engine applies its configured anti-spam interval before firing, but a listener doing anything expensive should still keep that in mind.

Seit:
1.0.0

  • Konstruktordetails

    • NpcInteractEvent

      public NpcInteractEvent(Npc npc, org.bukkit.entity.Player player, InteractionType interaction, org.bukkit.inventory.EquipmentSlot hand, org.bukkit.util.Vector clickedPosition)
      Creates the event.
      Parameter:
      npc - the NPC that was clicked
      player - the player who clicked it
      interaction - what the player did
      hand - the hand used, or null if the protocol did not say — an attack never reports one
      clickedPosition - where on the hit box the click landed relative to the NPC's feet, or null if the protocol did not say
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if npc, player or interaction is null

    • getClickedPosition

      public Optional<org.bukkit.util.Vector> getClickedPosition()
      Returns where on the NPC the click landed, relative to its feet.

      Only the interact-at form of the packet carries this, so a plain interact and an attack do not have it. Enough to tell a click on the head from one on the legs, which is how a plugin builds a hit-box-aware NPC.

      Gibt zurück:
      a copy of the offset, or empty if the protocol did not report one
